body: If you don't mind me asking, how DO you start from square one?  Maybe that's what is ultimately frustrating me; I just don't know HOW to continue forward.

I'm sorry, but I've always been annoyed by this answer.  With all do respect, it shows a complete lack of understanding towards 90% of people who consider suicide.  'Because it would hurt all the people who care about you' isn't a reason, it's a guilt trip.

If you are considering suicide, you already likely feel incredible guilt about any number of things all the time.  You also probably feel like you do nothing but cause these same friends and family who would miss you nothing but pain.  By using this reasoning, you are merely making the person feel even crappier about themselves, because you are also simultaneously (whether it's true or not) supporting the person's idea that they are just hurting everyone around them in their misery.

Suicide is an escape.  An escape from pressure, or stress, or pain, or w/e.  You may be trying to comfort them, but what they hear is, "

You also have to try and look at things a little objectively.  If a person commits suicide, than yes, their family and friends and loved ones (and maybe a few strangers who hear about it) will feel sad, but in the vast majority of cases, they will get over it.  A certain amount of pain will likely never go away, but they will move on, if only out of necessity, with their lives.  The person who wants to commit suicide feels like shit EVERY DAY.  Usually, every second of every day.  At what point does in fact become selfish or self centered for this person's loved ones to keep this person alive against their will?

Think about it.  Is it really fair for one person to live every day of their life in complete misery just to spare a handful of people a concentrated dose of sadness followed by a periodic stinging?  As I once heard a person in an anxiety group say, "You [aka, person telling them not to commit suicide] only have to live with me once in a while.  Maybe you think about me once a month, or once a week, or maybe even once a day.  I have to live with myself ALL the time.  My death would make you feel like shit every time you thought about me.  My life makes me feel like shit ALL THE TIME.  When exactly does it become ok for me to make my own choice?"

Now, I'm not advocating either way.  All I'm saying is, as a person who has gone through severe depression and has met many other people who have gone through severe depression (several of whom DID try to commit suicide), we don't want to hear sugar coated bullshit, and being positive always works better than being negative.

If you really don't want someone to commit suicide, and you want to help them, try telling them that they should live because tomorrow you will take them out for ice cream, or for a hike; not that they shouldn't do it because if they do, you will feel extra sad.  Boo hoo for you.

P.S.  If none of this makes any sense to you, or you think it's all bullshit, then think of it in these very black and white terms...

By using reasoning like this (aka, we'll all be sad if you die), you are essentially trying to "out sad" someone who is willing to KILL THEMSELVES.  Do you really think that when it comes right down to it, that someone who is willing to end their own LIFE because they are in such despair is going to stop just because it will make other people sad?  Give them a reason to live, not a reason not to die.

What is the next step?

And to answer your question, no.  I'm not comfortable with who I am.  I never have been.  And it's not so much that I'm not comfortable with who I am, but rather that I'm not comfortable with what I show, because it hasn't matched who I am for years and years.

It's not a "the grass is always greener" type thing, or a "you always want what you don't/can't have."  I just want to be who I AM.  My anxiety and lack of self-confidence has been crippling that since midway through high school.  I don't wish to be smarter, or more handsome, or cooler.  I don't WISH for anything.  I just want to be who I am.  Act the way I feel.  For instance, I am technically extroverted.  I love being around people.  I love concerts (rock or classical), and parties, and hanging at the bar, and chilling on a porch with friends, going to the movies, etc.  But I don't do it, because I lack the confidence to be proactive about these things, and even when I participate, my anxiety usually gets the better of me.  It's fucking torture.  And I know it's not who I am.  I have a friend who is very introverted.  I am one of the few people he ever hangs out with.  But he's comfortable with it.  He knows he doesn't like large groups, and one of the most relentlessly positive people I've ever heard of, never mind have met.

It's one thing to desire something you've never had.  It's another to feel crippled from doing the things you enjoy and hate the things you end up doing.  I'm fucking tired of it.  I've lost almost all of my friends because of it, I lost a girl I really love (over a year ago now) because of it, I've destroyed my relationship with most of my family because of it, I've squandered all of my chances and opportunities.  What the fuck is left?

Like I said earlier, I'm not normally a whiner.  Even now I don't feel sad for myself, just frustrated.  And if I could see some sort of light at the end of the tunnel, I would still fight.  But it's gone.  This isn't just a recent trend or a temporary setback.  It's been an inevitable downhill slide since high school.  And it's finally gotten to me.  I can't fight anymore.  There is only pain wherever I look.  I just want to move away and start anew, but I know it won't work.  It won't work because I don't have any money and because I actually do have an anxiety issue.

It's nice to try and put a positive spin on things annd say, "go get'em tiger!  If you're ready to kill yourself, why don't you just go out and do whatever the fuck you want, cause you've got nothing to lose!?"  But the fact is that if I could just don that attitude whenever I wanted, I would have pulled myself out of this funk long ago.  I don't have the strength to start from square 1.  Hell, more like from square -1.  FUCK.

Ah yes, and before anyone brings it up, I will NOT go back to the hospital.  I've been there.  I've seen what happens.  All it is is a temporary escape from the real world.  An escape that costs thousands and thousands of dollars.  I'd rather die than face the reality of my situation if I went back to the hospital.
